stimulus.text: The painting, attributed to Frederick Kemmelmeyer and made after 1795, shows George Washington on a white horse reviewing the Western Army at Fort Cumberland, Maryland. Washington points toward long ranks of soldiers in blue coats, with a cannon at the left and mountains behind them.
stimulus.source_note: Washington Reviewing the Western Army at Fort Cumberland, Maryland, attributed to Frederick Kemmelmeyer, after 1795, Metropolitan Museum of Art 63.201.2. Public domain.

primary_sources: Frederick Kemmelmeyer (attributed), Washington Reviewing the Western Army at Fort Cumberland, Maryland (after 1795)

stem: Washington’s response to the Whiskey Rebellion most directly showed what change from the years under the Articles of Confederation?

options.text: The president could now raise taxes without asking Congress.
options.misconception: The change was in enforcing the laws, not in who set the taxes.

options.text: The states could now refuse to send militia to the president.
options.misconception: Background: four states sent militia, so the states did not refuse the call.

options.text: The federal courts could now pardon rebels without a trial.
options.misconception: Background: the rebels were tried, and pardons came later; that was not the change shown.

options.text: The national government could now enforce its laws with military force.

rationales.D: Background: under the Articles, Shays’s Rebellion had to be put down by a privately paid militia, while Washington led nearly 13,000 militiamen in 1794.
rationales.A: Background: Congress still set the taxes; the change was in enforcing the laws.
rationales.B: The states sent the militia Washington called for.
rationales.C: Trials and pardons were not the change the painting shows.
rationales.general:
1. The painting shows Washington himself on horseback at the head of a large army.
2. Background: under the Articles, Shays’s Rebellion had to be put down by a privately paid militia because the national government had no force of its own.
3. Background: in 1794 Washington called up nearly 13,000 militiamen from four states and led them west himself.
4. So the response showed a national government that could now make its laws stick by force.
Remember: compare the response to the last rebellion; the difference is the new government’s power.
